key_terms.sense: attributing a found blood stain to another source
key_terms.definition: The principle that a woman who finds a blood stain may attribute it to another plausible source, such as another woman or an injury, and so remain pure herself.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The Gemara sets its limits: how likely the other woman must be to bleed, whether she may lose anything by it, and how women sharing a bed attribute blood to one another.

key_terms.sense: rabbinic impurity from a blood stain
key_terms.definition: A blood stain a woman finds on her body, clothing or an object without having felt a discharge. By rabbinic law it renders her impure as a niddah, subject to a number of leniencies.
key_terms.on_this_daf: R. Yehuda bar Livai rules that one may not attribute a stain to a woman who is impure only from a stain of her own (ein tolin ketem beketem), and Ravina rereads a baraita to preserve this rule.

key_terms.sense: a minor zavah awaiting one clean day
key_terms.definition: A woman who has a discharge on one or two days outside her menstrual period. She must observe one clean day for each day of discharge before immersing to become pure.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel lets the lender blame her on her second day, R. Yehuda HaNasi forbids it, and both allow it on her first day, when she loses nothing.

key_terms.sense: the postpartum days of pure blood
key_terms.definition: The period after childbirth and its initial impurity during which, by Torah law, blood a woman sees does not make her impure.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Attributing a stain to a woman in these days costs her nothing, so all agree it is allowed. Ravina reads the baraita's "woman keeping days" as such a woman.

key_terms.definition: A woman whose age and physical state allow menstrual bleeding, as opposed to one who is pregnant, nursing, elderly or too young, whose bleeding is presumed suppressed.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The first tanna and R. Meir dispute whether one may blame a gentile only if she has actually seen blood or also if she is merely fit to see. Women sleeping in one bed who are unfit to see may blame one who is fit.

key_terms.term: eino mekabel tum'ah eino mekabel ketamim
key_terms.hebrew: כל דבר שאינו מקבל טומאה אינו מקבל כתמים
key_terms.sense: no stain impurity on non-susceptible objects
key_terms.definition: R. Nechemia's rule that a blood stain found on an object that cannot become ritually impure, such as stone, earth or a tiny rag, does not make the woman impure.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Rav Mattana derives it from "clean she shall sit upon the ground". It is extended to the outside of an earthenware vessel and to small rags, and the halacha follows R. Nechemia despite the olive-leaf incident.
aliases: kol davar she'eino mekabel tum'ah eino mekabel ketamim

key_terms.sense: the brief time for bleeding to begin
key_terms.definition: The minimal span of time needed for the onset of menstrual bleeding. Blood found within it is treated as having been present at the moment the span began.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Rav requires the woman to check within this span for the others to be cleared, following Bar Padda's three periods linking the husband's offering to her taharot.
